acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT.

1. ARE THE DECLARED PREFIX FAMILIES SUFFICIENT FOR EVERY LATER CELL'S WRITES? NO -- AND THE GAP IS ALREADY VISIBLE IN THIS PROJECT'S OWN COMMITTED ARTIFACTS, WHICH IS WHY I CAN NAME IT RATHER THAN SUSPECT IT.
Declared: three families (intake, requests, generations) plus a firmless quarantine/, with the three generation artifacts -- vendor/report.pdf, sections/report.json, exports/{revision}/report.pdf -- nested UNDER firms/{firm_id}/generations/{id}/attempts/{a}/.
THE GAP: AN EXPORT THAT HAS NO GENERATION ATTEMPT HAS NO DECLARED HOME. B14 (IB-s-14) renders TWO export families. The ANALYSIS export descends from a YCharts generation attempt and is covered. The PERFORMANCE export is built from a PerformanceReport (B11) and a NarrativePacket (B13) and involves NO vendor generation at all -- there is no attempt id to nest it under, so the declared layout cannot express its location.
This is not a hypothesis. The two fixtures IB-s-18 committed at c4214773c9 and merged at 410f28f7db already disagree with each other: AnalysisReport.valid.json carries protected_pdf_ref.storage_key = 'firms/49financial/generations/REQ-0001/attempts/ATT-9/vendor/report.pdf', which matches the declared generations family EXACTLY; while ExportReceipt.valid.json carries storage_bucket 'opal-data-49f' and storage_key 'investor-reporting/exports/rev-3/report.pdf' -- A DIFFERENT BUCKET and a prefix this layout does not declare. A fixture is an illustration and not a destination decision, so neither is 'wrong'; what they show is that the destination question is UNSETTLED across this project's own artifacts and that IB-s-14 will have to settle it against a layout that currently answers only half of it.
A SECOND, SMALLER GAP: NarrativePacket has no declared home. B13's decomposition row names no S3 destination, so it may well live in irpt-requests; but ExportBundle pins 'narrative packet ... sha256', which implies a retrievable immutable artifact, and if that artifact is an S3 object it has no family.
A THIRD, DELIBERATE ONE: quarantine/ is FLAT. It carries no firm by design (a message reaches quarantine precisely when its firm could not be established), but it also carries no family, so a quarantined attachment and a quarantined message body share one prefix with no structure to tell them apart.
WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHY: I did not add a fourth family speculatively. IB-s-5 binds its FirmDestinationPolicy and its per-firm IAM conditions to WHATEVER THIS FILE DECLARES, so inventing a prefix here would silently widen the policy surface of a cell that has not been cut yet. Naming it is the act that belongs to this cell.

2. ONE BUCKET WITH IAM CONDITIONS, OR PER-FIRM BUCKETS? BOTH SHAPES ARE LIVE, AND THIS PROJECT NOW USES BOTH -- THAT IS THE FIRST THING THE CVO SHOULD KNOW.
data/firm_registry.json gives every firm its own bucket (opal-data-bd, opal-data-inf, opal-data-cot), so the per-firm shape is not hypothetical -- it is canonical for firm data. And row IRPT_BCKEND-S1 plus decomposition finding 1 already re-homed the directory and the holdings snapshot INTO the firm's own bucket. So after this cell: firm-derived DATA lives in per-firm buckets, and request EVIDENCE lives in one shared bucket with per-firm prefixes.
THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR THE SHARED BUCKET IS STRUCTURAL, NOT CONVENIENCE: QUARANTINE HAS NO FIRM. A per-firm bucket layout has nowhere to put an item whose firm could not be established, and choosing a bucket for it WOULD BE CHOOSING A FIRM -- the exact cross-firm write the ingestion gate exists to refuse. A shared bucket with a firmless quarantine/ prefix expresses 'unknown firm' directly, and no arrangement of per-firm buckets can. Second: the per-firm buckets are shared with other pipelines, so putting vendor artifacts and client mail attachments there widens what those buckets' EXISTING readers can reach; this bucket has exactly one producer set and one consumer set.
THE ARGUMENT AGAINST, AT FULL STRENGTH: CLAUDE.md section 5 pairs per-firm buckets with a bucket-scoped Deny, which is coarser and far easier to audit than a prefix condition. Three buckets fail SEPARATELY; one prefix condition is a single edit away from being wrong for all three firms at once, and the blast radius of a mistake in a shared bucket is every firm. That is a real asymmetry and it is not answered by the quarantine argument.
WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is not a matter of taste: whether IB-s-5's conditions can be shown to DENY cross-prefix access with a NEGATIVE test per firm (a principal scoped to 49financial refused on firms/inflection/). Until that test exists and passes, the shared bucket's separation is DESIRED and not EXERCISED. This cell created no policy at all, so today the separation is neither -- it is declared.
AN ASYMMETRY I DID NOT RESOLVE: the shared bucket is here because the PRD's paths row named it; the firm-bucket decision for directory and holdings came from a surprise row OVERTURNING a different PRD row. Two destinations, decided by two different mechanisms, in one project.

3. WHAT A READER OF layout.json CANNOT LEARN FROM IT. Eight things, and the first three matter most.
(i) WHO MAY WRITE ANYWHERE IN IT. The file declares WHERE, never WHO. No IAM condition, no bucket policy and no key-policy grant exists yet, so a reader who takes the per-firm prefixes as a separation GUARANTEE would be reading a declaration as a control.
(ii) RETENTION -- AND THERE IS NONE. This bucket has NO lifecycle rule, so vendor PDFs, client holdings attachments and every superseded version accumulate indefinitely. Nothing in the file hints at it, nobody declared it, and versioning (which this cell turned on for immutability) makes it strictly larger. I name it because it is a real standing property that no criterion in this order would have surfaced.
(iii) WHETHER ENCRYPTION IS ENFORCED. The file NAMES alias/investor-reporting, but the SSE default lives on the bucket; from the declaration alone a reader cannot tell an enforced default from an aspiration.
(iv) WHETHER ANY PREFIX HAS EVER BEEN WRITTEN. The declaration reads identically for a live prefix and one nothing has ever touched. Today, measured: 0 objects.
(v) THAT THE BRACES ARE PLACEHOLDERS. _meta.not_declared says so in prose, but a MACHINE reading firm_prefixes gets a string containing '{id}' and nothing typed tells it that is a variable.
(vi) ANY ORDERING OR LIFECYCLE between the families -- that an intake object precedes a request revision which precedes a generation attempt.
(vii) WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A FIRM IS REMOVED FROM THE REGISTRY: the next apply silently drops its prefixes from the declaration while its OBJECTS remain. The file is not a census of what exists and does not say so.
(viii) IT IS ONE LONG LINE. Terraform 1.9's jsonencode has no pretty-print, so a person needs `python -m json.tool` to read a file whose entire purpose is to be read. I chose terraform-managed generation over a hand-run generator because it makes registry drift a plan diff, and this is what that choice cost.
